draft.title: Earth's four spheres
card: the rock, soil and landforms of Earth, from the surface down through the crust. Carbon is stored here in rocks, coal and oil.
all living things, such as plants, animals and microbes, and the places where they live. Plants take in carbon dioxide from the air.
all the water on Earth, as liquid, ice and water vapour, including oceans, rivers and groundwater. Oceans absorb carbon dioxide from the air.
the layer of gases around Earth. Matter and energy move between all four spheres, so more carbon dioxide in the air can affect the oceans and living things.
draft.remember: Earth's lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere are linked, so extra carbon in the air affects the others.

a.q: Oceans, rivers and ice caps all belong to which of Earth's spheres?
a.why: The hydrosphere is all the water on Earth, in liquid, ice and vapour form. The lithosphere is tempting because oceans sit on the seafloor, but it is the rock and soil, not the water.
a.clue: Think about what each sphere is made of.

b.q: Heavy rain on a Victorian hillside washes soil into a creek. Which two spheres does the moving matter pass between?
b.why: Rain is water, so it is part of the hydrosphere. It moves soil, which is part of the lithosphere, into the creek. Biosphere is tempting because a hillside has plants, but the question is about the water and soil moving.
b.clue: Name what the rain is made of and what the soil is.
